title: Role Templates & Delegated Assignment Explorer
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Design a compact, discoverable UX for creating, previewing, and assigning role templates that supports delegated assignment workflows (tenant admins, team leads) and surfaces audit-significant choices. This work is part of RBAC v2 and focuses on the Console role editor and member assignment flows.

Background: Existing role editor is linear and verbose; admins often create near-duplicate roles for teams, then manually tune bindings. We need patterns to: (1) author parameterized role templates, (2) preview effective permissions for a given principal+resource, (3) enable delegated assignment with scoped constraints, and (4) clearly surface audit/logging implications (e.g., who granted, when, via which template).

Key user personas:
- Tenant Admin (primary): wants quick creation of standard roles, auditability, and safe delegation.
- Team Lead (delegated assigner): needs a constrained UI to assign pre-approved templates without exposing sensitive toggles.
- Security Reviewer (auditor): needs clear provenance and change history.

Primary flows to design:
1) Template Library: catalog of reusable role templates (search, filter by scope, last-updated, created-by). Templates show a compact permission fingerprint (read/write/exec on resource groups) and a brief human description.
2) Template Authoring: a guided editor to create templates from scratch or from an existing role. Supports parameter placeholders (e.g., ${team}, ${project}) and recommended guardrails (max privilege caps). The editor includes an automatic impact estimator: given a sample principal and resource, the UI simulates effective permissions.
3) Delegated Assignment Modal: a reduced-assurance modal for Team Leads with only allowed templates visible, additional optional fields (justification, expiry), and an inline audit notice describing where assignment will be recorded.
4) Assignment Preview & Audit Banner: before committing, a diff-style preview shows changes to the principal's effective permissions plus the exact audit event payload that will be logged (role_template_id, assigner, scope, expiry).

Design constraints & trade-offs considered:
- We must avoid leaking sensitive permission details to delegated assigners; therefore templates must support an "expose_details" flag for creators. Team Leads only see the fingerprint unless explicitly granted detail access.
- Template parameterization creates complexity for previews; we propose a required sample principal/resource during authoring to anchor the estimator, with a warning for untested parameter combinations.
- Performance: live permission simulation must be cached (server-side) to avoid console latency for large orgs.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Template Library mock exists in Figma with search/filter and card variants (compact/expanded).
- Authoring flow shows parameter placeholders and includes an impact estimator; prototype wired to simulated backend responses.
- Delegated Assignment modal shows restricted template list based on assigner role and includes justification + expiry fields.
- Preview shows permission diff and explicit audit payload; copy for audit banner approved by Security.
- Accessibility: keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels for template cards and preview diffs.

Open questions:
- Should templates be versioned automatically when edited, or should edits create a new template copy? (trade-off: provenance vs clutter)
- How granular should the template visibility rules be (tenant-wide vs project-scoped)?
- What retention/format for audit payload derivatives is required by compliance teams?
